Home Webinars How Collective Energy Shapes Performance WEBINAR How Collective Energy Shapes Performance Date: Thu., December 3, 2026 --> Time: 2:00 pm EST (New York) | 8:00 pm CET (Brussels / Paris) Time: --> Duration: 1 hour Register Now --> Date: Thu., December 3, 2026 Time: 2:00 pm EST (New York) | 8:00 pm CET (Brussels / Paris) Duration: 1 hour Register Webinar Begins days : hours : minutes --> Date: Thu., December 3, 2026 Time: 2:00 pm EST (New York) | 8:00 pm CET (Brussels / Paris) Duration: 1 hour Register Now Energy doesn’t add up between people, it multiplies. When a leader and their team bring strong, positive energy to an interaction, the combined effect can exceed what either brought alone. When one person’s energy is depleted, it can drag the whole interaction down. That dynamic, playing out across every interaction in an organization, is what creates collective energy: the pattern of where energy compounds, leaks, or gets blocked across a team or system. This insider session features our leadership energy research on more than 600 teams and 34,000 relational ties. You’ll learn why the vast majority of relationships at work are neutral or energizing, why the remaining 9% do outsized damage, why it takes 4 positive relationships to offset a single negative one, and why that effect triples when the source is the team leader. What You’ll Learn In this collective energy webinar, you’ll learn to: Explain why individual and relational energy multiply rather than add, and what that means for how organizations develop leaders Identify 6 behaviors that most consistently drain a team’s collective energy Apply 3 evidence-based strategies to protect and strengthen collective energy on your team Recognize the outsized role team leaders play in shaping collective energy, for better or worse Your Hosts Diane Bergeron, PhD Senior Research Scientist A social psychologist with over 20 years of experience, Diane is a researcher with expertise in executive education and consulting. Button Trauma-Informed Leadership: Balancing Support and Accountability for Struggling Team Members Wed, Dec 02 | Webinar Register Time & Location Dec 02, 2026, 12:00 PM – 1:00 PM EST Webinar About the Event Leadership conversations with team members who are not meeting expectations can be difficult for many reasons, such as not knowing what to say, being worried about their reaction, having a hard time with possible conflict, and more. Even when we prepare ahead of time, leaders may not always feel equipped to respond in the moment when team members share personal struggles (i.e., family concerns, trauma histories, grief/loss situations, etc.) that are impacting their ability to be present at work when we try to address our workplace concerns. Through discussion, real-world examples, and sample language/dialogue, this presentation will provide reframing of such conversations through a basic understanding of the nervous system and share a practical, trauma-informed sequence of engagement to navigate those times. The goal of this sequence of engagement is to create interactions that have the best chance of being resolved through both parties’ ability to reason and collaborate rather than get “stuck” in the emotional or reactive part of the brain. Participants will also be provided with handouts/tools that give example questions and statements they can tailor to their work. About our speaker Samantha P. Koury, EdD, LMSW, is one of the co-directors at The Institute on Trauma and Trauma-Informed Care (ITTIC), as well as a trainer and consultant. She is a graduate of the UB School of Social Work and has a doctorate in educational leadership and organizational innovation from Marymount University. Samantha has over a decade of experience working with leaders, organizations and systems to become more trauma- informed in their work. She is passionate about trauma-informed leadership, workforce wellness and helping organizations and systems plan for, implement and sustain trauma-informed change.
